narrative.northStar: A Swiss onchain fintech at base.org's craft, with registered ink plates on commit moments
narrative.overview:
The wallet reads like a technical fintech, not a crypto toy and not a private bank. White ground, ink type, and one fully saturated Swissquote orange that does real work: it fills the primary action, and fills the rising candles of the generative chart. The orange takes the place Base gives its blue. Warmth comes from that orange and from the apricot field that shows the worst case as an amount; precision comes from crisp corners, hairline borders and mono figures you can check against the chain.

Density is calm and single-column: one task per screen, the title at display size, then the facts. Live chain facts (network fee 0.00, the current Base Sepolia block, a live status square) sit beside the content as proof, never as decoration. Every moment where Face ID signs or something is committed onchain turns dark: an ink plate, registered by two crosshairs at opposite corners.

The system refuses both the purple-gradient crypto wallet and the beige private-bank page. Craft references are base.org (technical register, one committed colour, live facts, generative motion) and Phantom (warmth). The brand is a Swissquote-inspired prototype: the Swissquote name, its orange and the SQ monogram, no official assets.
keyCharacteristics: White and ink with one committed colour, Swissquote orange, which always carries ink text.
Hanken Grotesk for UI and display, tight and large; JetBrains Mono strictly for figures, addresses and status tokens.
Crisp corners (6 to 10px), hairline borders, flat surfaces: no shadows.
A generative, unlabelled candlestick chart on ink as the world's signature motion: orange rising candles, Plate Grey outlined falling ones, a crosshair under the pointer.
Ink plates registered by crosshairs for everything Face ID signs; the Account itself is an ink plate because it is live onchain.
Today's Face ID budget drawn as a row of ten square allowance cells that drain through the day and refill at 00:00 UTC.
Light by default; dark follows the OS.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Orange Rule
rules.body: An orange fill always carries ink text (accent-fg), never white. When orange must be read as text on a light ground, use Ember Ink.

rules.name: The One Committed Colour Rule
rules.body: Swissquote orange is the only brand hue. Green, red and amber are signals, never decoration, and there is no second accent.

rules.name: The Factor Code Rule
rules.body: The user's three factors keep one code on every screen: the phone (Face ID) is an orange-filled square, the cloud account an ink-outlined square, the Kit passphrase an ink-filled square. On an ink plate, ink translates to Plate White (filled Kit, outlined cloud); orange stays orange. No other colours encode factors, and the Swissquote guardian never gets a square because it is never an owner.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for figures, addresses, units and verifiable status. If the text is not a number, an address, a unit or a chain fact, it is set in Hanken Grotesk.

rules.name: The Amount Precision Rule
rules.body: An amount is shown at one of three precisions. Exact: what is given, received or signed shows to the last unit, up to six decimals ("0.498962 EURC"): the review hero, Allow, the receipt, the simulation preview and the typed confirmation (formatAssetExact, formatUsdcExact). Asset precision: balances, lists and quotes show two decimals for USDC and EURC and up to six for ETH, always rounded down so they never show more than there is (formatUsdc, formatAsset). Minimums are rounded down. Inputs take at most six decimals; Max fills the whole balance to the sixth decimal. Rates: a percentage with two decimals ("1.25%") with "variable" beside it, never a promised return; a swap rate reads "1 USDC = 0.9979 EURC".

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Titles are semibold at 1.05 line-height with negative tracking (-0.03 to -0.035em). Display size is for the one title per screen.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: No box shadows, no blurs, no glass. If something needs to stand out, it is either orange (action) or ink (commitment).

rules.name: The Ink Plate Rule
rules.body: A dark plate on a light screen means a factor (Face ID, the Kit) will sign this, or this is now live onchain. Never use it for marketing or general grouping.

rules.name: The Loss Bound Truth Rule
rules.body: The worst case is what is left today plus one daily limit per reset during the delay, computed exactly and shown with two decimals. Never "about", never rounded up for effect.

rules.name: The In-Row Panel
rules.body: Changing a rule opens under its own row, between the row's hairlines, with no border or card of its own; the row's control toggles Change ↔ Cancel and hides on the receipt. One panel is open at a time. The panel shows the worst case before → after on the apricot field before the review plate. The daily limit and the level upgrade follow it; the security key's panel will.

rules.name: Third-Party Powers
rules.body: Whenever a change gives an outside party a role on the Account, state its powers before signing: a hairline list of what it can do (ink check) and never can do (Graphite X), never green or red, then the trade-off in one muted line, above the plate.

dos: **Do** put ink text on every orange fill and use Ember Ink when orange has to be read as text.
**Do** show risk as a number before the user commits: limits, loss bounds and delays in mono figures on the apricot field.
**Do** put everything Face ID signs on an ink plate, with its crosshairs, as the last block before the action.
**Do** keep live chain facts (fee, block, live status) visible in the shell: the live strip on desktop, the token bar on phones.
**Do** use the Factor Code Rule squares whenever the phone, the cloud account and the Kit appear together.
**Do** draw today's Face ID budget as the ten allowance cells, with the remaining, the limit and the reset time beside them.
**Do** compute the loss bound exactly (what is left today plus one daily limit per reset) and lead its day squares with a "now" square.
**Do** show a refusal by the Account as evidence: the approval squares that signed, the outlined one that did not, and the Safe's code in mono.
**Do** call the device in hand "this device" in the lost-phone flow (it may be a laptop) and the other one "the old phone".
**Do** show what is given, received or signed exactly (up to six decimals), and balances, lists and quotes at the asset's precision, rounded down.
**Do** make every control at least 44px tall on phones, and step a big mono amount down a size before it would clip.
**Do** say which factors a payment needs in a sentence with approval squares, mono only for the figures.
**Do** show a rate as a percentage with two decimals and "variable", next to a footnote that it is a testnet rate and not promised.
**Do** mark the card or row in action with an ink border, and keep the screen's one orange fill for its primary action.
**Do** name an approved dApp with its short address in readable steps, and keep a transfer's recipient as the full address.
**Do** show a rule change as its worst case before → after on the apricot field, the current figure muted and the new one large, before the plate.
**Do** open a rule's change under its own row, inside its hairlines, with no card of its own, and give focus back to the row's control when it closes.
**Do** state a third party's powers before signing: a hairline list of what it can do (ink check) and never can do (Graphite X), above the plate.
**Do** answer a task that cannot run with a Gate Block: the situation as the title, one muted line, the way forward or "Close".
**Do** keep a power that is not built yet in place as a Soon slot: the neutral "Soon" badge beside its disabled small secondary button.
**Do** say who can do what as a powers matrix of factor squares and a few words, a table from 640px and a list on phones.

**Do** disclose any demonstration figure where it appears: a warning "Demo" badge on simulated screens and toys, and the demo timing in the row it changes ("7 days shown as 7 seconds", "a 3-minute delay").
**Do** use the tokens in `globals.css` and the kit in `web/src/components/ui`, never raw colours.
donts: **Don't** set white text on Swissquote orange.
**Don't** add box shadows, glass or blur; the card shadow token stays `none`.
**Don't** introduce a second accent, purple gradients, or a beige private-bank palette.
**Don't** use JetBrains Mono or uppercase tokens as a decorative kicker above a headline; tokens label data.
**Don't** round rectangles beyond 12px or turn markers into pills.
**Don't** give the Swissquote guardian a factor square; it is never an owner.
**Don't** colour a can / never-can list green and red; the check is ink, the X Graphite.
**Don't** set "Soon" or other non-data labels as mono tokens; use the kit's neutral badge.
**Don't** round a balance or a minimum up, or show a signed amount at list precision.
**Don't** let a plate row's label wrap; the value wraps.
**Don't** wrap a bordered panel's sections in cards of their own; separate them with hairline rules (plates, alerts and the Kit drop zone stay elements inside a section).
